h1: The 7 Best Bagged Canister Vacuums for Hard Floors, Carpet and Pets in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bagged Canister Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 bagged canister vacuums from Kenmore, Bissell and Eureka compared on HEPA, tools, brushrolls, bag supply and price.
summary: The Kenmore 81214 200 Series is the bagged canister to buy for most homes, with HEPA, a two-motor system and three tools at a mid-range price. The Kenmore 81414 400 Series adds a retractable cord and telescoping wand, the 600 Series is Kenmore's top tier, and the Eureka 3670M is the entry-level pick with bags included.
intro: People who buy a canister usually do it for one reason: they have hard floors, stairs or lots of furniture, and an upright keeps fighting them. The canister solves that by separating the motor from the hand, but it creates a new problem if you pick the wrong floor head. A canister with only a bare-floor nozzle will be poor on rugs, and one with only a motorised carpet head will scatter debris on tile.

So this ranking sorts seven bagged canisters on what travels with the machine: filtration, motor design, floor heads and brushrolls, tool set, cord handling and the supply of bags. We reviewed listings and specification sheets, not delivered vacuums, and we compare relative handling in place of weights the listings do not give.

products.name: Kenmore 81214 200 Series Pet Friendly Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum with HEPA, 2 Motor System
products.verdict: HEPA, a two-motor system and three tools at the lowest Kenmore price tier.
products.description:
Kenmore's 200 Series 81214 pairs pet-friendly design with a HEPA filter, dual motors and three included tools, for $100 to $200.

The two motors split the work: one produces suction, the other drives the powered floor head, which is why a canister can clean carpet properly. HEPA matters for a bagged machine because the bag already traps the bulk, and the filter catches the fine dust that passes it. It beats the dearer Kenmores on value, losing only on extras.

Buy it if you want HEPA and strong carpet cleaning without paying for extras. Skip it if you want a retractable cord.
products.idealFor: Mixed floors with pets or allergies.

products.name: Kenmore 81414 400 Series Pet Friendly Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum with Extended Telescoping Wand
products.verdict: HEPA, a telescoping wand, a retractable cord and four tools in one canister.
products.description:
The 400 Series 81414 has HEPA, an extended telescoping wand, a retractable cord and four cleaning tools. It costs $200 to $500.

The extended wand matters for tall users and for stairs, because a fixed wand forces you to stoop. The retractable cord ends the winding chore. It sits just behind the 200 Series since the added price buys convenience more than cleaning power.

Buy it if you value reach and cord convenience. Skip it if you want to spend less.
products.idealFor: Tall users and homes with stairs.

products.name: Kenmore 600 Series Pet Friendly Bagged Canister Vacuum
products.verdict: Kenmore's top canister tier, built around pet households.
products.description:
The 600 Series pet friendly canister sits at the top of Kenmore's canister range and costs $200 to $500. The listing offers few specifics beyond the top-tier positioning and pet focus.

Higher series numbers in appliance lines usually mean better build, more tools and quieter operation, but with no detail on the listing we cannot say what the 600 adds over the 400. That uncertainty is why it sits behind the better-documented models.

Buy it if you want Kenmore's top tier and pet focus. Skip it if you want documented specs.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want Kenmore's top range.

products.name: Kenmore 600 Series Bagged Canister Vacuum with Hair Eliminator Brushroll
products.verdict: A canister with a hair-eliminator brushroll that resists tangles.
products.description:
This 600 Series canister is fitted with a Hair Eliminator brushroll and costs $200 to $500.

Brushrolls clog with hair, and clearing them is the chore people hate most. A design that resists wrap saves that cutting-and-pulling job, which matters for long-haired owners and pets. It ranks fourth because it shares the same price as better-documented siblings.

Buy it if hair tangling is your main complaint. Skip it if you rarely vacuum carpet.

products.name: Kenmore Pet Friendly Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: A light pet-friendly canister with sealed, low-exposure bag disposal.
products.description:
This Kenmore is a lightweight pet-friendly bagged canister with sealed disposal, priced at $200 to $500.

Sealed disposal is the quiet advantage of bagged machines: you lift out the bag and the dust goes with it, with little exposure. For allergy sufferers that matters more than a bagless bin dumped into a can. It ranks fifth because the listing gives no motor or HEPA detail.

Buy it if low-exposure dust disposal matters to you. Skip it if you want a documented feature list.
products.idealFor: People who want low-exposure dust disposal.

products.name: Bissell Zing Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum, Purple, 2154A
products.verdict: An inexpensive bagged canister with the reach of the format.
products.description:
The Bissell Zing 2154A is a lightweight bagged canister at $50 to $100.

It delivers the canister essentials: a bag, a hose and wand, and the reach to go under furniture. Detail on motors, HEPA and tools is absent from the listing. It ranks sixth because at this price you accept fewer features.

Buy it if you want canister reach for the least money. Skip it if you want HEPA or a full kit.
products.skipIf: You want HEPA or a full kit.

products.name: Eureka 3670M Canister Cleaner, Lightweight Powerful Vacuum for Carpets and Hard Floors, with 5 Bags
products.verdict: An entry-level canister for carpets and hard floors, with five bags in the box.
products.description:
The Eureka 3670M is a lightweight canister for carpets and hard floors that includes five bags. It costs $50 to $100.

Bag supply is a running cost, so a box that includes five bags is a useful start. Eureka is a long-standing vacuum brand and bags for this style are easy to find. It ranks last because the listing lists no HEPA or motor details.

Buy it if you want an entry canister with bags included. Skip it if filtration is a priority.

whatMatters.detail: A canister needs the right head for the floor: a bare-floor head for tile and wood, a powered head for carpet. Powered heads need a motor, which is why two-motor systems matter. Check that the head matches your floors.
A sealed bag traps most dust, and a HEPA filter catches the fine particles that escape. For allergy sufferers the pair works well. Check that the filter is true HEPA on the listing.
Hair wrap on a brushroll is a common complaint. Hair eliminator designs reduce it. If you have long-haired people or pets, check for the feature.
A telescoping wand adjusts to your height and a retractable cord removes winding. Both are convenience features, not cleaning power. Decide how much they are worth.
Bags are an ongoing cost, so look at availability and price. Many popular Kenmore and Eureka bag types are easy to find. Buy a multi-pack to save.

faq.q: Why choose a bagged canister over bagless?
faq.a: Bags contain dust at disposal and suit allergy sufferers. Bagless saves the cost of bags but exposes you to dust when you empty the bin.
Using the wrong head. A bare-floor head on carpet cleans poorly, and a powered head on delicate floors can scatter debris.

faq.q: Is the 81414 worth it over the 81214?
faq.a: If you want the retractable cord and extended wand, yes. For pure cleaning value, the 81214 is better.
Insert a bag, attach the hose and wand, choose a head and plug in. It takes a couple of minutes.

faq.q: How often do I change the bag?
faq.a: When it is about two-thirds full or suction drops. Full bags reduce airflow.
No. Use the bag type listed for your model, as the wrong size can leak dust.

finalTake: For most homes, the Kenmore 81214 200 Series is the best bagged canister vacuum: HEPA, a two-motor system and three tools at a sensible price. The 81414 adds reach and a retractable cord, the 600 Series with the Hair Eliminator suits long-haired households, and the Eureka 3670M is the budget start. Match the head to your floors, and keep spare bags in a drawer.
